data.speaker: support
data.text:
Connectivity troubleshooting, step by step:
First, check your internet connection. Make sure you’re actually online, and if you’re on Wi‑Fi, verify you’re connected to the right network.
Next, restart your router. Power it off, wait a few seconds, then power it back on and let it fully reconnect.
Finally, clear your browser cache. Then try the connection again.

Login troubleshooting, step by step:
First, verify your username and password. Type them carefully and use the exact values you set.
Next, check caps lock. A single uppercase letter can make the login fail.
Finally, try a password reset if you’re still blocked, then log in with the new password.

Performance troubleshooting, step by step:
First, close unused applications. Freeing up memory and CPU can help a lot.
Next, clear temporary files. This can reduce clutter and improve responsiveness.
Finally, restart your device to reset resources and apply any stuck changes.

core_changes: Content.from_realtime_event(kind=...) and a 'realtime_event' ContentType: Content's constructor accepts the unknown type at runtime, but ContentType and Content.from_dict's type check (_types.py:2047) reject it, so a serialised update with realtime-event content wouldn't round-trip.

FunctionInvocationContext.realtime_conversation: set by an internal function middleware the conversation always installs, because _auto_invoke_function builds the context itself and only passes a context to tools without middleware when the tool declares a ctx parameter.

Content.from_text(status=): Content() already takes status, and text merges keep the latest status (_types.py:2142), so only the factory keyword is missing. The prototype calls Content('text', status=...).
